sec-transport-mariadb-clients.why: goes DONE. FreeScout is the only client not encrypted, and ce457cb2 moves its CA to the image's ENV_* .env passthrough, which the env-watcher follows with a config:clear — so the CACHE rebuilds with the CA. If this stays not-encrypted:freescout, the passthrough is a fourth allow-list and the doctrine §5.3 conclusion is incomplete.

notify-supersede.why: restated:39 -> roughly restated:36. drift-watch fires nightly and now declares security-drift-verdict, so its 3 predecessors retire. os-resume (30) needs a machine wake and backup-verify (5) the next drill — neither is due tonight, so a drop to 0 would mean something I have not predicted.

sec-transport-pg.why: stays DONE, saying `encrypted`. It is the control: nothing in this converge touches PostgreSQL clients, so a change here is a sampling artefact or a regression, and either is worth more than the green.

sec-transport-hedgedoc.why: stays DONE. Its answer comes from HedgeDoc's own kernel, not a sample, so unlike sec-transport-pg it should not be able to flap at all. If it does, the self-test is not as deterministic as claimed.

sec-transport-mysqld-exporter.why: stays `plain`. Nothing was written for it. A change would mean somebody edited the exporter outside the repo — which is how two services went down on 2026-08-23.
